title: review: S2a v2: route a provider="claude" row (id claude:<tier>) through the existing Claude fallback path with the row's tier
spec:
Goal T-1334 (S1 T-1352 merged). Replaces T-1356 after spec review T-1358 (reservation keyed on the row id, tier=row id leaking into t["tier"] readers, missing review_rule, unreleased reservation on early returns). New design: a Claude executor row's id is "claude:" with an alias in [models] (e.g. id "claude:opus"). That id is exactly the executor value the existing fallback path already writes (spawn.py:1564 f"claude:{tier}"), so dispatch reuses executor._exhausted()'s tested machinery (account pick, reservation handoff to run_worker, review_rule, running_claude_workers counting) with the row's tier instead of fallback_tier(complexity). t["tier"] stays a real [models] alias; spawn.run_worker is unchanged. 1. orchestrator/pool.py Pool._read_executors (uses executor_rows from S1): a provider="claude" row is valid only if its id is "claude:", tier in ("haiku","sonnet","opus"), cfg["models"][tier] is a str, and its model is absent or equal to cfg["models"][tier] (absent -> set to that value). An invalid claude row is loaded with enabled=False and hold_reason "invalid claude row: ", plus one stderr line; never raise at load. 2. orchestrator/executor.py _exhausted(pool, t, run=None, tier=None): tier None keeps today's behaviour exactly (policy + fallback_tier). tier given (routed claude row): skip the on_exhausted policy check, use that tier, same pool.pick("execute") (None -> held, hold_reason "no account with headroom"), same bus.update(tier=tier, fallback="claude", review_rule=...), same thread + reservation handoff. 3. executor.start (executor.py:487): if ex is not None and ex.provider == "claude": ex.roll_day(); ex.day_tasks += 1; pool.save(); result = _exhausted(pool, t, tier=ex.id.split(":", 1)[1]); handed_off = result.get("status") == "fallback"; return result. elif ex is None or ex.provider == "codex"-unavailable: unchanged. Any other provider -> held, hold_reason "unknown executor provider

" (release as the finally already does). 4. No change to spawn.py, run_worker, reservation code, review routing or t["tier"] readers: all already handle "claude:". Tests (unittest.TestCase methods): start with only a claude:opus row eligible calls the worker with an account_id, sets tier "opus" and fallback "claude", and pool.executors["claude:opus"].day_tasks increments; routed dispatch ignores on_exhausted="hold"; no account headroom -> held; invalid claude rows (bad id, unknown tier, model mismatch) load disabled with the reason; a valid row without model gets cfg models[tier]; existing tests/test_executor.py _exhausted cases unchanged. No pool.toml edit, no new dependencies. Additive; git revert restores Codex-only routing.

result.summary: The diff matches the spec: claude rows are validated at load, routed dispatch goes through _exhausted with the row's tier, and unknown providers are held. Named tests are present and the gate was green. The two comments below are minor and non-blocking. I did not read the test bodies, only the pool.py and executor.py hunks.

comments.issue: day_tasks is incremented and saved before _exhausted runs. If it then holds for no headroom, the row is charged a day task for a dispatch that never started. The spec orders it this way, so this is only a budget-accounting inaccuracy.

Saved state cannot overwrite hold_reason on an invalid claude row, but it still overwrites the enabled flag if state ever stores one. EXEC_STATE_FIELDS does not include enabled, so this is safe today. The guard is a prefix string match, which is fragile.
